name: CagriSema
used_for: Developed by Novo Nordisk as a once-weekly injectable combination for weight management in adults with overweight or obesity. Unlicensed sellers also offer the two peptides together.
summary: CagriSema is a fixed combination of cagrilintide (an amylin analog) and semaglutide (a GLP-1 receptor agonist) under study by Novo Nordisk. A new drug application was filed with FDA on 18 December 2025 according to the company, and no approval was found as of this review; no FDA statement on it could be read. Phase 3 trials of the combination exist (for example REDEFINE 1, NCT05567796), unlike the other blends. The detailed information is on the pages for Cagrilintide and Semaglutide; formulations vary by seller.

side_effects.text: In REDEFINE 1, gastrointestinal adverse events were more frequent with CagriSema than placebo (79.6% versus 39.9%) and were mostly mild to moderate.
side_effects.label: research

research.summary: REDEFINE 1: phase 3 trial (Novo Nordisk, started November 2022, about 3,400 participants) of once-weekly CagriSema in people with overweight or obesity, listed as active, not recruiting with results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov.
research.finding: Primary outcomes were relative change in body weight and achievement of at least 5% weight reduction at week 68 versus placebo.

research.summary: Coadministered cagrilintide and semaglutide in adults with overweight or obesity (N Engl J Med; REDEFINE 1, 68-week phase 3 trial).
research.finding: Weight change was -20.4% with CagriSema versus -3.0% with placebo, with gastrointestinal adverse events in 79.6% versus 39.9%. Funded by Novo Nordisk.

research.summary: REDEFINE 2: 68-week phase 3 trial of CagriSema versus placebo in 1,206 adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes (N Engl J Med; NCT05394519).
research.finding: Weight change was -13.7% with CagriSema versus -3.4% with placebo; gastrointestinal events were 72.5% versus 34.4%.
